title: Academic WorldQuest 2026-27 — The Tug of War on Natural Resources
format: Multiple choice, four options; 'answer' gives the correct option letter
sources: R1: UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) — Critical minerals, critical decisions: Industrial policy for the energy transition
R2: CSIS — Greenland, Rare Earths, and Arctic Security (Schwartz & Baskaran, 8 Jan 2026)
R3: East Asia Forum — Policies that enable China's critical minerals edge (David Landry, 12 Mar 2026)
R4: Council on Foreign Relations — The Global Water Crisis: Stress, Scarcity, and Conflict (updated 20 Mar 2026)
R5: Chatham House — The rare earths race risks environmental disaster (Patrick Schröder, 3 Mar 2026)
R7: NPR — Countries are negotiating rules to mine the deep sea. The U.S. is pushing ahead alone (13 Mar 2026)
R8: CFR Education — What Is Water Scarcity? (updated 31 Mar 2026)

questions.question: In 2024, which country supplied nearly three-quarters of global cobalt output?
questions.explanation: UNCTAD cites the DRC's dominance as an example of highly concentrated production.

questions.question: Which two countries accounted for more than two-thirds of global nickel production in 2024?
questions.explanation: Indonesia and the Philippines together produced over two-thirds of the world's nickel.

questions.question: Which two countries together represented over half of global lithium production in 2024?
questions.explanation: Australia and Chile produced more than half of the world's lithium.

questions.question: The so-called 'lithium triangle' consists of which three countries?
questions.explanation: Lithium reserves are concentrated in the triangle and in Australia, but refining is concentrated in China.

questions.question: According to UNCTAD, China accounts for roughly what share of global rare earth mining output?
questions.explanation: China mines about 70% of rare earths and controls more than 85% of refining and separation capacity.

questions.question: In 2022, refined cobalt averaged $20.8 per kg. What was the average price of raw cobalt?
questions.explanation: Refined lithium, graphite, nickel and cobalt sold for three to four times the price of raw forms.

questions.question: UNCTAD's main lesson from the lithium value chain is that positions are shaped by what?
questions.explanation: Reserves sit mainly in South America and Australia, yet China dominates refining.

questions.question: In UNCTAD's rapid assessment project, stakeholders in which African country identified procurement policies, standards enforcement and skills development as ways to link mining with domestic manufacturing?
questions.explanation: Namibian stakeholders separately emphasized training centres, industrial infrastructure and SME support.

questions.question: What does UNCTAD identify as the key challenge for mineral-rich developing countries?

options.B: Turning resource endowment into structural transformation rather than enclave-type extraction

questions.explanation: UNCTAD argues market forces alone will not deliver inclusive outcomes; integrated industrial policy is needed.

questions.question: On January 5, 2026, President Trump said the US needs Greenland for what reason?
questions.explanation: CSIS says the renewed focus reflects the administration's view of resource security as national security.

questions.question: Greenland ranks where in the world for rare earth reserves, with 1.5 million tons?
questions.explanation: Greenland ranks eighth, though no rare earth mining has yet taken place.

questions.question: What are the names of Greenland's two large rare earth deposits?
questions.explanation: Both lie near the town of Narsaq on Greenland's southern tip.

questions.question: Roughly what share of Greenland is ice-free?
questions.explanation: Only 20% is ice-free, and temperatures can fall below -40°F.

questions.question: In June 2025, the US Export-Import Bank sent a letter of interest for a $120 million loan to fund which project?
questions.explanation: If approved, it would be the Trump administration's first overseas investment in a mining project.

questions.question: In 2018, China launched an Arctic policy, known as the Polar Silk Road, in which it controversially called itself what?
questions.explanation: Most Chinese projects in Greenland have been blocked over security concerns.

questions.question: Which Chinese rare earth company is the second-largest shareholder in the Kvanefjeld mine?
questions.explanation: Shenghe signed an MOU in 2018 to lead processing and marketing of Kvanefjeld's output.

questions.question: What is the northernmost US military installation, located in Greenland?
questions.explanation: Pituffik (formerly Thule Air Base) provides missile detection, missile defense and space surveillance.

questions.question: If the Northwest Passage becomes open every summer, it would connect East Asia and Western Europe with a route about how much shorter than the Panama Canal route?
questions.explanation: Greenland's position along this route gives it strategic importance.

questions.question: Why has Greenland repeatedly denied an exploitation license to the Kvanefjeld project?

options.A: Its ore grade is too low
options.C: It is on a military base

questions.explanation: About 270,000 tons of uranium are co-located there, making it the world's eighth-largest uranium deposit.

questions.question: Greenland's 2021 election, widely known as the 'mining election,' was won by which party, which then banned mining of deposits with high uranium concentrations?
questions.explanation: The ban applies to deposits above 100 ppm uranium; Kvanefjeld has about 300 ppm.

questions.question: Energy Transition Minerals is demanding $11.5 billion in compensation over the uranium ban — nearly how many times Greenland's 2023 GDP?
questions.explanation: The company argues the ban amounts to expropriation; Greenland's GDP was $3.3 billion in 2023.

questions.question: Greenland is three times the size of Texas. How many miles of road does it have?
questions.explanation: Inadequate transport and energy infrastructure impede mining development.

questions.question: In 2018, Denmark blocked a Chinese state-owned company from building airports in Greenland after urging from which US official?
questions.explanation: Denmark pulled the bid and financed much of the airport upgrades itself.

questions.question: In June 2025, the EU designated which Greenland project as a Strategic Project under its Critical Raw Materials Act?
questions.explanation: GreenRoc Mining received a 30-year exploitation license for Amitsoq in December 2025.

questions.question: In 2024, China accounted for roughly what share of global graphite production?
questions.explanation: China has since imposed multiple rounds of graphite export restrictions.

questions.question: To build local support, the Tanbreez project committed to sourcing what share of its workforce locally?
questions.explanation: CSIS contrasts Tanbreez's community engagement with Kvanefjeld's local opposition.

questions.question: In early 2024, the ten largest publicly traded Chinese mining companies paid about 3.7% effective interest on debt. What did the ten largest foreign miners pay?
questions.explanation: Subsidised credit lets Chinese firms out-invest and outlast rivals.

questions.question: How many of China's 100 largest mining companies are at least partly state-owned?
questions.explanation: Government stakes in those 94 firms average close to 80%.

questions.question: According to East Asia Forum, China accounts for roughly what share of world copper refining?
questions.explanation: Landry cites about 45% for copper, 70% for lithium and 90% for rare earths.

questions.question: Chinese firms hold stakes in at least how many active overseas mining properties?
questions.explanation: State-owned enterprises hold stakes in about 60% of these, often in higher-risk jurisdictions.

questions.question: Simandou, a giant iron ore deposit now roughly two-thirds controlled by Chinese firms, is located in which country?
questions.explanation: Guinea has received more than US$27 billion in Chinese financial commitments since 2010.

questions.question: Which mining company spent heavily exploring Simandou before being partially expropriated in 2008?
questions.explanation: Rio Tinto later sold 47% of Blocks 3 and 4 to a Chinese consortium led by Chinalco.

questions.question: Average Chinese ownership stakes in overseas mines rose from about 60% in 2002 to over what level in 2022?
questions.explanation: Chinese firms shifted from minority stakes and joint ventures to outright acquisitions.

questions.question: Which industrial policy 'carrot' has China used to favor domestic processing over raw mineral exports?
questions.explanation: VAT incentives channel minerals into China's processing and manufacturing ecosystem.

questions.question: By around 2015, China's mining sector was the second-most 'compliant' sector in embedding what in corporate governance?
questions.explanation: Only public utilities ranked higher; the committees ensure strategic priorities shape major decisions.

questions.question: Profit margins for Chinese firms refining battery metals hover around what level, according to a Huayou Cobalt executive?
questions.explanation: Thin margins push refiners to outbid rivals for raw materials, letting Chinese miners earn up to 40%.

questions.question: Japan recently became the first to attempt raising rare earth-rich seabed mud from what depth in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.explanation: Chatham House cites it as the starkest example of the race reaching extreme frontiers.

questions.question: According to the US Geological Survey, which region holds an estimated 21 billion tonnes of rare earth reserves, second only to China?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is also biodiverse, climate-critical and near Indigenous territories.

questions.question: Every tonne of rare earths mined can generate up to how many tonnes of toxic waste?
questions.explanation: The waste includes radioactive material, alongside millions of tonnes of wastewater a year.

questions.question: Which Chinese city, a hub for in-situ leaching of rare earths, is known as the 'Rare Earth Kingdom'?
questions.explanation: Ganzhou in Jiangxi Province suffers severe soil acidification and water contamination.

questions.question: Which radioactive element is found in waste from the Bayan Obo rare earth sites in Inner Mongolia?
questions.explanation: Waste discharged into tailings reservoirs such as the Weikuang Dam contains thorium and heavy metals.

questions.question: Chatham House says community consultation should follow which principle articulated in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples?
questions.explanation: FPIC is presented as a prerequisite for social licence to operate.

questions.question: According to a 2024 Benchmark assessment, only what share of rare earth producers comply with the Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management?
questions.explanation: Chatham House calls for stronger enforcement and aligning financing with recognized standards.

questions.question: In January 2026, the Trump administration announced a $1.6 billion public investment in which company?
questions.explanation: Chatham House argues such investments should be conditional on high environmental standards.

questions.question: What dynamic does Chatham House warn multilateral coordination is needed to prevent in the rare earths race?

options.A: A 'race to the bottom' on environmental safeguards
options.C: A collapse in rare earth prices

questions.explanation: In the rush to reduce dependence on China, safeguards may be weakened, repeating past mistakes.

questions.question: What are the potato-like lumps on the deep ocean floor that contain cobalt, nickel and manganese called?
questions.explanation: A baseball-sized nodule can take about 3 million years to form.

questions.question: Which company plans a deep-sea mining project in international waters between Hawaii and Mexico?
questions.explanation: It proposes a large seabed 'vacuum cleaner' to collect nodules and hopes to start commercial mining next year.

questions.question: Independent scientists found that right after test mining, what share of seafloor life was gone?
questions.explanation: That figure excludes animals living on the nodules themselves.

questions.question: Which US agency reduced environmental review for deep-sea mining after a Trump executive order?
questions.explanation: NOAA says faster permits will help supply the US with vital minerals.

questions.question: The International Seabed Authority, which is writing rules for access to deep-sea minerals, meets in which country?
questions.explanation: The US says it is not subject to those rules, a stance critics say undermines its own interests.

questions.question: Casper, highlighted by NPR as a species threatened by nodule mining, is what kind of animal?
questions.explanation: Casper lays eggs on sea sponges that grow only on nodules; it has no scientific name yet.

questions.question: In a January 2026 report, UN researchers said the world has entered an era of what?
questions.explanation: Overwithdrawal has damaged water systems to the point that repair is impossible or prohibitively costly.

questions.question: More than how many people worldwide lack adequate access to clean water, according to CFR?
questions.explanation: The problem is projected to worsen with population growth and climate change.

questions.question: Roughly what share of the world's freshwater is used for agriculture?
questions.explanation: Industry uses less than 20% and domestic uses around 12%.

questions.question: Under the Falkenmark Water Stress Indicator, 'absolute scarcity' means less than how many cubic meters of renewable freshwater per person per year?
questions.explanation: Stress is below 1,700 and scarcity below 1,000 cubic meters.

questions.question: What type of water scarcity occurs when communities lack the money and technology to use available water?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia, with no permanent rivers, uses its wealth for desalination to overcome physical scarcity.

questions.question: Groundwater supplies about what share of domestic water use globally?
questions.explanation: It also supplies over 40% of irrigation water and is being depleted faster than it replenishes in many regions.

questions.question: According to Bloomberg, about what share of new data centers built or in development since 2022 are in water-stressed areas?
questions.explanation: CFR cites data centers as high-water-use projects that compound scarcity.

questions.question: According to UNICEF, how many of the world's twenty most water-scarce countries are in the Middle East and North Africa?
questions.explanation: MENA is considered the region most vulnerable to water scarcity.

questions.question: Gulf states are nicknamed 'saltwater kingdoms' because of their reliance on desalination. Which country relies on it for 99% of its drinking water?
questions.explanation: Qatar is the Gulf country most dependent on desalination.

questions.question: According to the Pacific Institute, how many water-related conflicts occurred in 2024, a record?
questions.explanation: Its Water Conflict Chronology has recorded more than 2,750 incidents over thousands of years.

questions.question: Which dam on the Blue Nile does Egypt say could drastically reduce its share of the river's water?
questions.explanation: Egypt claims most of the Nile's water under colonial-era treaties that upstream states reject.

questions.question: What term have some experts used for Russia's deliberate destruction of Ukraine's water infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Aquacide is the deliberate destruction, contamination or weaponization of water resources.

questions.question: Iranian officials accused the US of striking a desalination plant on which Persian Gulf island, cutting water to thirty villages?
questions.explanation: US officials denied responsibility.

questions.question: Which four countries established the Senegal River Basin Organization in 1972 to jointly manage hydraulic infrastructure?

options.C: Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso and Senegal
options.D: Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia and Sierra Leone

questions.explanation: CFR cites it as an example of cooperative transboundary water management.

questions.question: In 2023, historically low water levels caused by drought forced authorities to restrict ship traffic through which waterway?
questions.explanation: CFR uses it to show how water stress disrupts global trade.

questions.question: Which Sustainable Development Goal aims to 'ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all'?
questions.explanation: UN-Water coordinates international efforts toward Goal 6.

questions.question: Where will the United Nations host a Water Conference in December 2026?
questions.explanation: It will focus on water cooperation, multilateral governance and investment.

questions.question: Which country's law requires water utilities to reinvest part of their profits in green infrastructure?
questions.explanation: The US and Canada have provided tens of millions of dollars to support Peru's efforts.

questions.question: Transboundary waters account for what share of the world's freshwater flows?
questions.explanation: UN-Water says 60% of freshwater flows cross national boundaries.

questions.question: How many countries have territory within at least one transboundary river or lake basin or aquifer system?
questions.explanation: There are 286 transboundary river and lake basins and 592 transboundary aquifer systems.

questions.question: How many of the 153 countries sharing transboundary waters have operational arrangements covering 90% or more of them?
questions.explanation: Only 43 countries have such comprehensive arrangements (UN-Water, 2024).

questions.question: At least how many countries lack any arrangements for sharing transboundary waters?
questions.explanation: At least 20 countries have no arrangements at all.

questions.question: Between 2020 and 2023, how many countries improved cooperation with neighbors on transboundary water resources?
questions.explanation: UN-Water reports only eight countries improved cooperation in that period.

questions.question: Which UN legal framework for transboundary water cooperation does UN-Water cite in calling for a 'source-to-sea' approach?

options.A: UN Convention on the Law of the Sea

questions.explanation: Parties must protect links between land, freshwater and marine environments.

questions.question: UN-Water warns that depleted coastal aquifers can allow what to happen?

options.A: Saltwater intrusion and higher concentrations of arsenic and fluoride

questions.explanation: Upstream activities can jeopardize coastal resources across borders.

questions.question: In June 2020, Egyptian hackers infiltrated twelve government websites of which country over a dam dispute?
questions.explanation: The hack protested Ethiopia's dam on the Nile's largest tributary.

questions.question: About how many people live with severe water scarcity for at least one month each year?
questions.explanation: That is roughly half the world's population; about half a billion face year-round scarcity.

questions.question: What share of Earth's water is salt water and therefore not drinkable?
questions.explanation: Of the 3% that is fresh water, only about one-third is readily accessible.

questions.question: Which country holds more than half of Africa's water reserves, yet over one-third of its population lacks adequate water access?
questions.explanation: CFR Education attributes this to infrastructure issues and resource mismanagement.

questions.question: Research suggests the global economy loses how much each year due to inadequate clean water and sanitation?
questions.explanation: The figure reflects lost time and money spent obtaining clean water.

questions.question: How much clean drinking water does the United States lose every day to leaky, decades-old pipes?
questions.explanation: Crumbling infrastructure threatens urban water supplies.

questions.question: Which city almost ran out of water in 2017, reallocating agricultural water and contributing to the loss of thirty thousand farming jobs?
questions.explanation: The move saved the city but harmed farmers' livelihoods.

questions.question: Records from 650 BCE describe a king from which empire drying up an enemy's wells?
questions.explanation: CFR Education uses it to show water conflict is as old as recorded history.

questions.question: Australia spent $3.5 billion to build a desalination plant that now supplies about one-third of which city's water?
questions.explanation: Desalination plants remain expensive to build and energy-intensive to run.

questions.question: Orange County, California, has reduced its drought risk by recycling more than how much wastewater per day?
questions.explanation: Treated sewage is reused for purposes such as toilet flushing and irrigation.
